reasoning: The automated text extraction was largely successful, with high programmatic recall and precision. However, the LLM fidelity analysis identified three major defects: an OCR error that alters a date in the document's watermark, a structural failure where parts of a numbered list were converted to plain paragraphs, and the visual duplication of the agency logo at the beginning of the document. These major defects trigger a mandatory human review.

concerns.description: Minor text differences beyond acceptable reformatting
concerns.analysis: There is a minor text difference that alters a date. The large diagonal watermark on Page 1 of the source document clearly reads 'Approved 2/10/2022' (which is consistent with the watermark dates on the subsequent pages), but the output extracts this text as 'Approved 2/25/2022', likely due to an OCR error caused by the table lines intersecting the text.

The source document contains a continuous numbered list running throughout the document. While items 1-4 on page 2 are converted as a list, items 6, 7, 8, and 9 on page 3 are incorrectly converted into plain text paragraphs with the numbers manually included in the text (e.g., '**6. 2022 Technology Committee Goals**'). This violates the requirement that numbered lists must use proper list elements rather than paragraph tags.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: 6. 2022 Technology Committee Goals – The proposed 2022 Technology Committee Goals were discussed.
concerns.output_quote: **6. 2022 Technology Committee Goals** – The proposed 2022 Technology Committee Goals were discussed.

concerns.analysis: The HTML output visually duplicates the single agency logo found on the first page of the source PDF. The pipeline has extracted two variations of the same logo (one smaller, one larger, with slightly different alt text) and placed them consecutively at the very beginning of the HTML document, causing the logo to render twice to the end user.
